leaks.lede: A pack has seconds to work. Each stage below is where packs lose that moment, and how we design for it.

stages.why: A pack is judged next to its neighbours. What stands out depends on what surrounds it.
stages.does: We study the category shelf and marketplace listings, so the pack is designed to be seen among real competitors.

stages.breaks: Choosing a box because it is cheap or standard.
stages.why: Shape and material affect how a pack feels, how it protects the product and what it costs to ship.
stages.does: We design structure and materials around the product, protection, shipping cost and the feeling you want when it is opened.

stages.breaks: Giving every message the same weight.
stages.why: When brand, product, variant and claims all shout, none is read.
stages.does: We set a clear order of information, so a shopper sees the brand, understands the product and finds the variant at a glance.

stages.breaks: Judging the pack only at full size.
stages.why: Most first impressions now happen on a phone screen, where the pack is a thumbnail.
stages.does: We test packs at thumbnail size and on marketplace and quick-commerce tiles, so they stay clear when small.

stages.breaks: Sending artwork to print without checks.
stages.why: Colour, dielines and label information are easy to get wrong, and costly to reprint.
stages.does: We prepare print-ready artwork, check colour and dielines, and leave room for the label information your product requires.
